facts.statement: The genus Hypacrosaurus was described by Brown in 1913.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1913

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The name Hypacrosaurus means "near the highest lizard" because the animal was almost as large as Tyrannosaurus but slightly smaller.
facts.quote: Hypacrosaurus (meaning "near the highest lizard" [from Ancient Greek ὑπο- hypo- "less" and ἄκρος akros "high"], because it was almost but not quite as large as Tyrannosaurus)

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus possessed a tall, hollow, rounded crest similar to Corythosaurus, though it was less large and straight than that species' crest.
facts.quote: Like Corythosaurus, it had a tall, hollow rounded crest, although not as large and straight.

facts.statement: Remains of Hypacrosaurus species date from 75.0 to 69.5 million years ago and were found in Alberta, Canada, and Montana, United States.
facts.quote: It is known from the remains of two species that spanned 75.0 to 69.5 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, and Montana, United States

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus remained an obscure genus until 1987, when nests, eggs, and hatchlings of H. stebingeri were discovered in the Bear Paw Formation.
facts.quote: It was an obscure genus until the discovery in 1987 of nests, eggs, and hatchlings belonging to H. stebingeri in the Bear Paw Formation.

facts.statement: The type remains of Hypacrosaurus were collected in 1910 by Barnum Brown for the American Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: The type remains of Hypacrosaurus were collected in 1910 by Barnum Brown for the American Museum of Natural History.

facts.statement: The type skeleton (AMNH 5204) consisted of several vertebrae and a partial pelvis found along the Red Deer River near Tolman Ferry, Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: The remains, a partial postcranial skeleton consisting of several vertebrae and a partial pelvis (AMNH 5204), came from along the Red Deer River near Tolman Ferry, Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: Barnum Brown described the remains as a new genus in 1913, considering it similar to Saurolophus.
facts.quote: Brown described these remains, in combination with other postcranial bones, in 1913 as a new genus that he considered to be like Saurolophus.

facts.statement: Although no skull was known when the genus was first described, two skulls were discovered and described shortly afterward.
facts.quote: No skull was known at this time, but two skulls were soon discovered and described.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus had neural spines projecting from the top of its vertebrae that were 5 to 7 times the height of the vertebral bodies, giving it a tall back in profile.
facts.quote: The neural spines, which project from the top of the vertebrae, are 5 to 7 times the height of the body of their respective vertebrae in the back, which would have given it a tall back in profile.

facts.statement: The skull crest of Hypacrosaurus was more pointed on top, shorter, wider side-to-side, and had a small bony point at the rear compared to Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: The skull's hollow crest is like that of Corythosaurus, but is more pointed along its top, not as tall, wider side to side, and has a small bony point at the rear.

facts.statement: Unlike other lambeosaurines, the airway passages in the crest of Hypacrosaurus altispinus did not form an S-curve.
facts.quote: Unlike other lambeosaurines, the passages for the airways do not form an S-curve in the crest (at least not in H. altispinus).

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus is estimated to have been around 9.1 meters long and weighed up to 4.0 tonnes.
facts.quote: The animal is estimated to have been around 9.1 m long, and to have weighed up to 4.0 tonnes (4.4 tons).

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus was a bipedal and quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Like other duckbills, it was a bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus had a grinding motion analogous to chewing, with teeth packed in dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, though only a few were in use at any time.
facts.quote: Its skull permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus cropped plants with a broad beak and held them with a cheek-like organ, feeding from the ground up to about 4 meters above.
facts.quote: Plant material would have been cropped by its broad beak, and held in the jaws by a cheek-like organ. Its feeding range would have extended from the ground to about 4 m above.

facts.statement: The hollow crest of Hypacrosaurus likely served social functions, such as visual signaling for sex or species identification and acting as a resonating chamber for noises.
facts.quote: The hollow crest of Hypacrosaurus most likely had social functions, such as a visual signal allowing individuals to identify sex or species, and providing a resonating chamber for making noises.

facts.statement: The crest and nasal passages of Hypacrosaurus are subjects of debate regarding dinosaur endothermy and the presence of nasal turbinates.
facts.quote: The crest and its associated nasal passages have also figured in the debate about dinosaur endothermy, specifically in discussions about nasal turbinates.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus is classified as a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid.
facts.quote: Hypacrosaurus was a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid, and has been recognized as such since the description of its skull.

facts.statement: Within the Lambeosaurinae, Hypacrosaurus is most closely related to Lambeosaurus and Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: Within the Lambeosaurinae, it is closest to Lambeosaurus and Corythosaurus

facts.statement: Michael K. Brett-Surman suggested in 1989 that Hypacrosaurus and Corythosaurus might be the same genus.
facts.quote: Michael K. Brett-Surman (1989) suggesting that Hypacrosaurus and Corythosaurus are the same genus.

facts.statement: While Suzuki et al. (2004) suggested Hypacrosaurus might be paraphyletic, later analyses rejected this, finding the two species form a clade with Corythosaurus and Olorotitan as closest relatives.
facts.quote: Although Suzuki et al.s 2004 redescription of Nipponosaurus found a close relationship between Nipponosaurus and Hypacrosaurus stebingeri, indicating that Hypacrosaurus may be paraphyletic, this was rejected in a later, more comprehensive reanalysis of lambeosaurines, which found the two species of Hypacrosaurus to form a clade without Nipponosaurus, with Corythosaurus and Olorotitan being the closest relatives.

facts.statement: The two species of Hypacrosaurus are not differentiated by unique characteristics because H. stebingeri was described as transitional between Lambeosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: The two known species, H. altispinus and H. stebingeri, are not differentiated in the typical method, of unique characteristics, as H. stebingeri was described as transitional between the earlier Lambeosaurus and later Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: The species Hypacrosaurus stebingeri was described by Horner and Currie in 1994.
facts.quote: subdivision: Hypacrosaurus stebingeriHorner & Currie, 1994

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus lived approximately between 75 and 67 million years ago.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente entre 75 a 67 millones de años

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: durante el Maastrichtiense y Campaniense

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus fossils have been found in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Oxygen-isotope ratios suggest Hypacrosaurus was a homeotherm and likely endothermic, though this contradicts earlier findings based on nasal turbinates.
facts.quote: Oxygen-isotope ratios calculated for Hypacrosaurus suggesting that the ratios varied little, indicating that Hypacrosaurus was a homeotherm, and likely was endothermic.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus stebingeri laid roughly spherical eggs containing embryos that were 60 cm long.
facts.quote: Hypacrosaurus stebingeri laid roughly spherical eggs of 24 by, with embryos 60 cm long.

facts.statement: Hatchlings of Hypacrosaurus were approximately 1.7 meters long.
facts.quote: Hatchlings were around 1.7 m long.

facts.statement: Research suggests Hypacrosaurus stebingeri reached reproductive maturity at 2 to 3 years and full size at 10 to 12 years.
facts.quote: Research by Lisa Cooper and colleagues on H. stebingeri indicates that this animal may have reached reproductive maturity at the age of 2 to 3 years, and reached full size at about 10 to 12 years old.

facts.statement: The growth rate of Hypacrosaurus stebingeri was faster than that of its tyrannosaurid predators like Albertosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The postulated growth rate of H. stebingeri outpaces those of tyrannosaurids (predators of hypacrosaurs) such as Albertosaurus and Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: Secondary cartilage has been discovered in the skull of a Hypacrosaurus stebingeri hatchling.
facts.quote: Secondary cartilage has been found in the skull of a hatchling specimen of H. stebingeri.

facts.statement: Tooth marks on a Hypacrosaurus fibula show it was preyed upon or scavenged by tyrannosaurids in the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The discovery of tooth marks in the fibula of a Hypacrosaurus specimen inflicted by a bite from the teeth of a tyrannosaurid indicated that this, and other hadrosaurids were either preyed upon or scavenged by large theropod dinosaurs during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: A large group of Hypacrosaurus stebingeri in Montana died from a volcanic ashfall.
facts.quote: The large, monospecific assemblage of Hypacrosaurus stebingeri in Montana was interpreted as a group of dinosaurs that was killed by a volcanic ashfall.

facts.statement: The cause of death for the Hypacrosaurus assemblage was suffocation by ash and volcanic gases.
facts.quote: The cause of death in a volcanic ashfall is suffocation by the ash and by the gases released from volcanic eruptions.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus altispinus lived in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation alongside Edmontosaurus and Saurolophus.
facts.quote: H. altispinus shared the Horseshoe Canyon Formation with fellow hadrosaurids Edmontosaurus and Saurolophus

facts.statement: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation environment had significant marine influence from the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation is interpreted as having a significant marine influence, due to an encroaching Western Interior Seaway

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus altispinus may have preferred to live in more landward areas away from the seaway.
facts.quote: H. altispinus may have preferred to stay more landward.

facts.statement: The Two Medicine Formation, home to H. stebingeri, was higher, drier, and more terrestrial than the Horseshoe Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: This formation was more distant from the Western Interior Seaway, higher and drier, with a more terrestrial influence.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus belongs to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus is part of the tribe Corythosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Corythosaurini

facts.statement: Cheneosaurus and Procheneosaurus are considered synonyms for Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: CheneosaurusLambe, 1917 ProcheneosaurusMatthew, 1920 (en parte)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Hypacrosaurus was warm-blooded, with some researchers arguing it was not based on the absence of nasal turbinates.
facts.quote: This is in contrast to the Ruben et al. (1996) finding that Hypacrosaurus was not warm-blooded, which was based on the absence of nasal turbinates

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus was a duck-billed dinosaur genus that looked similar to Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: Era un género del dinosaurio de pico de pato similar en aspecto a Corythosaurus.

facts.statement: It had a tall, hollow, rounded crest that was not as large or upright as that of Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: Como este último, tenía una cresta redondeada alta y hueca, aunque no como grande y erguida.

facts.statement: Remains of two species are known from Alberta, Canada, and Montana, USA.
facts.quote: Se conoce por restos de dos especies que vivieron en Alberta, Canadá, y Montana, los EE. UU.

facts.statement: It can be distinguished from other crested duck-billed dinosaurs by its high neural spines and crest shape.
facts.quote: Hypacrosaurus es fácil de distinguir de otros picos de patos con crestas por sus altos procesos espinosos en la vértebras y la forma de la cresta.

facts.statement: Its neural spines projecting from the back vertebrae were 5 to 7 times higher than the body of the respective vertebra.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales, que se proyectan en dorsal de las vértebras de la espalda son de 5 a 7 veces más altas que el cuerpo de la respectiva vértebra.

facts.statement: The animal measured around 9.10 meters in length and had an estimated weight of 4 tons.
facts.quote: El animal media alrededor de 9,10 metros de largo, y un peso estimado de 4 toneladas.

facts.statement: Like other hadrosaurs, it was a herbivore that alternated between bipedal and quadrupedal positions.
facts.quote: Como otros hadrosáuridos era un herbívoro que altenaba entre la posición bípeda y cuadrúpeda.

facts.statement: The holotype remains were collected in 1910 by Barnum Brown for the American Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: Los restos del holotipo de Hypacrosaurus fueron recogidos en 1910 por Barnum Brown del Museo Norteamericano de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: The holotype consisted of postcranial vertebrae and pelvis parts (AMNH 5204) found near Tolman Ferry, Alberta, in rocks now known as the Horseshoe Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: Los restos, un esqueleto postcraneal consisten en varias vértebras y partes de la pelvis, AMNH 5204, provenientes de las riberas del Río Red Deer cerca de Tolman Ferry, Alberta, Canadá, rocas que hoy son conocidas como pertenecientes a la Formación Cañón Herradura.

facts.statement: Brown described these remains along with other postcranial bones, which were considered a new genus Saurolophus in 1913.
facts.quote: Brown describió estos restos, conjuntamente con otros huesos postcraneales, que en 1913 fueron considerados un nuevo género Saurolophus.

facts.statement: The generic name comes from Greek words meaning "less," "high," and "lizard," because it was smaller than Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico proviene de la combinación de los vocablos en griego υπο, hypo, "menos", ακρος, akros, "alto" y σαυρος saurus "lagarto", debido a que era más pequeño que Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The new species was named based on a variety of remains, including juveniles with associated eggs and nests, found in the Two Medicine Formation of Montana and across the border in Alberta.
facts.quote: La nueva especie Hypacrosaurus fue nombrada para una variedad de restos, incluyendo crías con huevos asociados y nidos, encontrados en la Formación Dos Medicinas de Montana, y a través de la frontera en Alberta.

facts.statement: These remains represent the largest collection of skeletal baby material of any known hadrosaurid species.
facts.quote: Estos representan "la colección más grande de material esquelético del bebé de cualquier especie conocida de hadrosáurido".

facts.statement: It was a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid, recognized as such from the description of its skull.
facts.quote: Hypacrosaurus fue un hadrosáurido lambeosaurinae, siendo reconocido como tal desde la descripción de su cráneo.

facts.statement: Michael K. Brett-Surman suggested in 1989 that Hypacrosaurus and Corythosaurus are the same genus.
facts.quote: Michael K. Brett-Surman en 1989, sugiriendo que Hypacrosaurus y Corythosaurus son el mismo género.

facts.statement: A 2012 study placed Hypacrosaurus altispinus closer to Olorotitan than to Hypacrosaurus stebingeri, which would suggest Hypacrosaurus is paraphyletic if confirmed.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2012 de Prieto-Márquez y colegas coloca a Hypacrosaurus altispinus más cercano a Olorotitan que a Hypacrosaurus stebingeri, lo que de confirmarse volvería a plantear la parafilia de Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: Its skull allowed chewing-like movement, and its teeth were continuously replaced in batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a handful functional at the same time.
facts.quote: El cráneo permitía un movimiento análogo a la masticación, y sus dientes se substituían continuamente y estaban incluidos en baterías dentales que contuvieron centenares de dientes, solo un puñado eran funcionales al mismo tiempo.

facts.statement: The vegetation it would have eaten ranged from the ground up to 4 meters high.
facts.quote: La vegetación de la que se habría alimentado abarcaba desde el suelo hasta los 4 metros de alto.

facts.statement: Tooth marks on the fibula of a Hypacrosaurus specimen inflicted by a tyrannosaurid bite indicate it was prey or eaten as carrion by large theropod dinosaurs during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de marcas de dientes en el peroné de un espécimen de Hypacrosaurus infligido por una mordedura de los dientes de un tiranosáurido indicó que este y otros hadrosáuridos fueron presa o comidos como carroña por grandes dinosaurios terópodos durante el Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Hypacrosaurus is paraphyletic; Suzuki et al. suggested a strong relationship between Nipponosaurus and H. stebingeri in 2004, but Evans and Reisz rejected this in 2007, finding the two species form a separate clade from Nipponosaurus but with Corythosaurus and Olorotitan.
facts.quote: Suzuki et al. en la redescripción del 2004 de Nipponosaurus encontró una fuerte relación entre Nipponosaurus y Hypacrosaurus stebingeri, indicando que posiblemente Hypacrosaurus sea parafilético, Esto ha sido rechazado por Evans y Reisz en 2007, en un más intensivo reanálisis de los lambeosaurinos, donde se encuentra que las dos especies de Hypacrosaurus forman un clado separado de Nipponosaurus, pero junto de Corythosaurus y Olorotitan.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus stebingeri laid spherical and rough eggs measuring 20 by 18.5 centimeters containing embryos 60 centimeters long.
facts.quote: H. stebingeri ponía huevos esféricos y rugosos de 20 por 18,5 centímetros con embriones de 60 centímetros.

facts.statement: Research by Lisa Cooper and colleagues suggests Hypacrosaurus stebingeri could have reached reproductive maturity at 2 to 3 years old and maximum size between 10 to 12 years old.
facts.quote: Investigación de Lisa Cooper y colegas sobre H. stebingeri indica que este animal pudo haber alcanzado madurez reproductiva en la edad de 2 a 3 años, y aproximadamente alcanzando el tamaño máximo entre los 10 a 12 años.

facts.statement: The postulated growth rate for Hypacrosaurus stebingeri was faster than that of tyrannosaur predators like Albertosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: El índice de crecimiento postulado para H. stebingeri era más veloz que el de los tiranosáuridos, depredadores de Hypacrosaurus, por ejemplo Albertosaurus y Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: A large, single-species group of Hypacrosaurus stebingeri in Montana was interpreted as a herd killed by a volcanic ash fall.
facts.quote: El gran conjunto monoespecífico de Hypacrosaurus stebingeri en Montana fue interpretado como un grupo de dinosaurios que fue muerto por una caída de ceniza volcánica.

facts.statement: The hollow crest of Hypacrosaurus likely served social functions, such as visual signaling for sex or species identification and providing a resonance chamber for sounds.
facts.quote: La cresta hueca de los hipacrosaurios tenía muy probablemente funciones sociales, tales como una señal visual permitiendo que los individuos identifiquen el sexo o la especie, y proporcionando un compartimiento de resonancia para hacer ruidos.

facts.statement: Ruben and others concluded in 1996 that nasal turbinates were absent in Hypacrosaurus based on CT scans, though this was not considered evidence that the animal was cold-blooded.
facts.quote: Ruben y otros en 1996 concluyeron que los turbinados nasales no estaban presente en Nanotyrannus, Ornithomimus o Hypacrosaurus basados en escaneo CT, aunque esto no es evidencia que estos animales fueran de sangre fría.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus belongs to the subfamily Corythosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Corythosaurini

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The genus Hypacrosaurus was named by Brown in 1913.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus altispinus lived alongside various other dinosaurs including hadrosaurs, ankylosaurs, nodosaurs, ceratopsids, pachycephalosaurs, ornithomimids, and tyrannosaurs in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: H. altispinus encontrado en la formación Cañón Herradura se ha hallado junto a otros hadrosáuridos como Edmontosaurus y Saurolophus, el hipsilofodóntido Parksosaurus, el anquilosáurido Euoplocephalus, el nodosáurido Edmontonia, ceratópsidos como Montanoceratops, Anchiceratops, Arrhinoceratops, y Pachyrhinosaurus, el paquicefalosáurido Stegoceras, los ornitomímidos Ornithomimus y Struthiomimus, y una variedad de pocos conocidos pequeños terópodos como trodóntidos y dromeosáuridos, y los tiranosáuridos Albertosaurus y Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: Hypacrosaurus stebingeri lived in the Two Medicine Formation alongside the nesting hadrosaur Maiasaura and the troodontid Troodon.
facts.quote: La formación Dos Medicinas, hogar de H. stebingeri, también poblado por el hadrosáurido también conocido por los nidos, Maiasaura, el trodóntido Troodon, quien también se conoce por restos de nidos.
